site/privacy.html.content:
Lux Omni

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 13 October 2026

Lux Omni (“Luxy”) is a browser-based project maintained by Luxraj Kayal (Subrata Kayal). It includes a workspace for supported files and an optional Dropbox connection. In the current build, PDF editing and export are not connected; a source PDF should not be overwritten unless an edited PDF export is supplied and you explicitly choose Sync. This policy explains how the website handles information when you use it.

Information used by the Dropbox integration

If you choose to connect Dropbox, Luxy requests permission to read file metadata, download file contents, and upload file contents. It uses these permissions to list supported files and download a file you select. For PDFs, an upload back to the selected file’s original Dropbox path is only intended when an edited PDF export is available and you explicitly press Sync. PDF editing and export are not connected in the current build, so Sync cannot replace the source with edited PDF content until an exported PDF is supplied.

Luxy may process the selected file’s name and Dropbox path, plus the PDF contents you choose to open. Dropbox provides authentication and the storage APIs; your Dropbox account and files remain subject to Dropbox’s own terms and privacy policy.

Where information is processed and stored

  • Luxy is a static website hosted through GitHub Pages. The current application does not send PDF contents to a Luxy-operated application server or store them in a Luxy-operated database.
  • The Dropbox access token is held in this browser tab’s sessionStorage for the active session, rather than localStorage. Browser session restoration can vary; do not use the app on a device you do not trust.
  • Selected PDFs are downloaded to the browser for viewing. The selected Dropbox path is kept in memory for the active page session.
  • If a future or connected editor supplies an exported PDF and you use Sync, that exported PDF is sent to Dropbox using overwrite mode and may replace the original file. The current build does not connect PDF editing/export. Keep a backup whenever the original must be preserved.

Lux Omni Clipboard history

Lux Omni Clipboard can keep up to ten recent items in this browser's local IndexedDB storage. Entries are ordered with the newest first and may contain text you copy using the Text Clipboard's Copy text button, images you copy using the Screenshot Clipboard's Copy screenshot button, or selected text you explicitly save using “Save to Temporary Log” from the Lux Omni page’s right-click menu. Older entries are automatically removed when the history exceeds ten items.

This history feature does not continuously monitor or record everything you copy elsewhere on your device. Selected text is saved only after you select it, right-click within Lux Omni, and explicitly choose “Save to Temporary Log”; clipboard items are recorded when you explicitly use a Copy button within Lux Omni Clipboard. The selected text is stored in this browser profile and is not sent to a Lux Omni-operated server by this feature. Importing a history item does not create a new history entry until you copy it again. Use Clear history to remove the stored entries, or clear this website’s browser data to remove locally stored records.

Third-party services

Luxy uses Dropbox for OAuth authorization and file API requests, cdnjs to load the Dropbox JavaScript SDK, and GitHub Pages to host the website. Those services may process standard connection or operational data under their own policies. Luxy does not currently include its own analytics service or user-account system.

Your choices and security

Connecting Dropbox is optional. You can decline authorization. To revoke ongoing access, review and disconnect Luxy from your Dropbox account’s connected-app settings. Closing the browser tab usually ends the tab’s session storage, but revoking access in Dropbox is the clearest way to remove the app’s authorization. Never share your access token or use Sync unless you intend to replace the selected Dropbox file.

Project names, branding, and authorship

The Lux Omni project and its related tools and features are associated with the project author, Luxraj Kayal (Subrata Kayal). Project and product names used or contemplated within this project include:

  • Lux Omni
  • Lux Omni Clipboard
  • Lux PDF Viewer
  • Lux PDF Editor
  • Lux Player
  • Lux Viewport
  • Lux Markdown
  • Lux Docs
  • Luxy, and related names or variants used for Lux Omni project tools, modules, and features

These names identify or are intended to identify this project and its related tools, and are attributed to Luxraj Kayal (Subrata Kayal) as the project author. To the extent applicable, the author reserves rights in original project materials and project-specific branding, including original code, writing, artwork, icons, and design. This notice does not claim exclusive ownership of generic words or names, third-party brands or products, external services, libraries, or content. Any rights in those third-party materials remain with their respective owners and are subject to their applicable terms and licenses.

Changes to this policy

This policy may be updated if Luxy’s features or data handling change. The “Last updated” date above will be changed when a revision is published.

Questions or privacy concerns: open an issue in the Luxy repository. Please do not post access tokens, private documents, or other sensitive information in public issues.

README.md.content:
# Lux Omni

Lux Omni is a browser-based workspace created by **Luxraj Kayal (Subrata Kayal)**.

## Current features

- **Dropbox connection:** connect to Dropbox through the browser, browse supported files, and open a selected file.
- **Workspace viewports:** open a full-screen viewport or a resizable split-screen layout; minimize, restore, or close viewports.
- **YouTube playback:** load a YouTube video into a workspace viewport.
- **Display controls:** switch between light and dark themes and enable Focus Mode.
- **Lux Omni Clipboard:** switch between Text Clipboard, Screenshot Clipboard, and Log List; edit and copy text, paste or choose an image to preview and copy, and import entries from the ten most recent text/image copy actions stored locally in the browser.

## Current application status

The current build includes the interface and Dropbox integration. The PDF workspace still uses a browser preview placeholder; a complete PDF editing, annotation, and export engine is not connected. Features should be understood from the current implementation rather than assumed from the product name.

## Run locally

Python 3 can serve the static website for local preview. From the repository root, run:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory site
```

Then open [http://localhost:8000/](http://localhost:8000/).

Dropbox authentication requires the redirect URI used by the local address to be allowed in the Dropbox app configuration. The integration uses a browser-based OAuth flow and requires a supported browser environment.

## Project files

- `site/index.html` — main Lux Omni interface.
- `site/app.js` — interface interactions, themes, Focus Mode, and viewport behavior.
- `site/styles.css` — main interface styling.
- `site/dropbox-integration.js` — Dropbox connection and file selection logic.
- `site/clipboard.html` — standalone Lux Omni Clipboard page.
- `site/privacy.html` — privacy policy for the current website.
- `PROJECT-GOALS.md` — product requirements and development decisions.

## Project documentation

- [Copyright notice](COPYRIGHT.md)
- [License and rights notice](LICENSE)
- [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)
- [Privacy policy](site/privacy.html)
- [Project goals](PROJECT-GOALS.md)

## Ownership and third-party materials

Original first-party Lux Omni software and project materials are attributed to **Luxraj Kayal (Subrata Kayal)** and are subject to the terms in [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party components are not claimed as first-party work and remain subject to their respective owners' licences and notices; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

Access to this repository and use of GitHub features are subject to GitHub's terms. Those platform permissions do not grant a general licence to reuse first-party material outside applicable permissions.

## Contact and project issues

For a project issue, use the [GitHub Issues page](https://github.com/LuxrajKayal/Luxy/issues). Do not post private documents, access tokens, or other sensitive information in GitHub issues.

PROJECT-GOALS.md.content:
# Lux Omni — Living Project Goals

Last updated: 2026-10-12

This is the working source of truth for the product direction agreed by the project owner. It is intentionally a living document: goals may change, but do not silently reinterpret or replace an owner's decision. Update this file only when the owner explicitly changes or approves a decision.

## 1. Product identity and ownership

- **Product name:** Lux Omni
- **GitHub repository:** `LuxrajKayal/Luxy`
- **Project owner / intended author of first-party work:** Luxraj Kayal, also known as Subrata Kayal.
- The product is being developed as a real product intended for users and eventual commercial distribution, not merely as a coding exercise.
- Attribute original first-party product work to the project owner. Do not claim that third-party library authors authored the Lux Omni application, and do not claim ownership of third-party code.

The first-party rights notice for original Lux Omni materials is recorded in the root `LICENSE` and `COPYRIGHT.md` files. Third-party software intentionally loaded by the current application is identified in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`; its own licence terms remain separate from the first-party terms.

## 2. Long-term product direction

The intended product path is:

1. Build and refine the **standalone web-based application** first.
2. After the website-based product has a solid foundation, discuss and plan external website integration features with the owner.
3. Implement both intended embedding approaches as future features:
   - **Iframe embedding:** allow a website to display the hosted Lux Omni application in an iframe.
   - **Web Component integration:** allow a website to incorporate a Lux Omni custom element, with a documented integration API.
4. Later, revisit adapting the product into a Chrome extension and commercial distribution.

Iframe embedding and Web Component integration are both part of the product's intended feature set, but **neither is part of the initial development scope**. The order, API, permissions, security model, packaging and implementation details remain undecided until discussed with the owner.

## 3. Current phase: website-based interface

**Current priority: work on the website-based application interface.**

- Proceed one small, reviewable step at a time.
- The owner decides the interface design, layout, colors, toolbar, panels, icons, labels, wording, branding and interactions.
- Do not invent or finalize product-facing text or visual design without approval.
- Discuss one material design or architecture decision at a time.
- Do not begin iframe support, Web Components, Chrome extension packaging, Google Drive OAuth, or unrelated features merely because they are long-term goals.
- Keep the product architecture understandable and modular where useful, but do not overbuild for future features before the current scope requires it.
- The website implementation approach and module boundaries must be discussed when relevant. Do not add a third-party UI framework or build dependency without explaining the trade-offs and obtaining approval.

### Approved initial PDF/Markdown interaction

These behavior decisions were explicitly approved by the owner:

1. **PDF-first start:** The application starts in its PDF workspace. The Markdown editor is not open by default.
2. **Dedicated open action:** Provide a new Markdown Editor button/action in the PDF workspace. The exact label and presentation remain subject to the owner's interface decisions.
3. **Side-by-side after opening:** When the user activates the Markdown Editor action, show the PDF panel and Markdown editor panel side by side by default.
4. **User-resizable panels:** The user can resize the two panels to suit their needs.
5. **Separate panel controls:** The PDF panel has controls appropriate to PDF viewing and annotation; the Markdown panel has its own controls appropriate to Markdown editing and saving. Do not merge their toolbars or assume that one panel's controls apply to the other.
6. Further behavior—such as panel collapsing, remembering sizes, mobile layout, Markdown formatting controls, and save/Save As behavior—remains undecided and must be discussed when relevant.

The visual design details (exact header, placement, dimensions, colors, icons, toolbar layout, and panel styling) are not finalized by these behavior decisions. Do not invent them.

## 4. Independent development — strict separation from prior repositories

- This project starts from zero in `LuxrajKayal/Luxy`.
- Do not copy, fork, clone, transplant, rename or reproduce source code, interface, wording, comments, documentation or project structure from the old `Luxraj-PDF` or `pdf-annotation-test` repositories, or from another PDF editor.
- The old `Luxraj-PDF` repository may be inspected for observation or high-level comparison only. It is not a template or source for implementation.
- Prior conversation code must not be silently reused.
- Feature descriptions are requirements only; they are not permission to copy another implementation.
- If a proposed approach resembles a previously observed project, make decisions based on requirements and independently reasoned engineering choices, not by transplanting that project's design or code.

## 5. First-party work and dependencies

- Original Lux Omni source code, project documentation, and original assets are attributed to the project owner where created by or rightsfully owned by the owner.
- Only describe a third-party library as used by the application when it is intentionally loaded or integrated into the current build.
- The current application loads the Dropbox JavaScript SDK. Its version and MIT licence notice are recorded in the root `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- Do not add another third-party library, framework, CDN, external service, authentication provider, or build dependency without first explaining its purpose, boundaries, licence, alternatives, and limitations, then receiving the owner's approval.
- Keep first-party work separate from third-party material. Preserve required third-party copyright and licence notices for software intentionally used or distributed.
- Do not claim ownership of third-party code or misrepresent what is actually integrated and tested.
- Do not describe PDF editing, export, or other components as complete without code evidence and suitable testing.

## 6. Working method

For each step:

1. Explain the immediate decision or problem plainly.
2. Present options and trade-offs when the decision is material.
3. Wait for the owner's decision before making that decision on their behalf.
4. Identify the intended repository and exact scope before edits.
5. Make only the approved changes.
6. Inspect the actual diff and run suitable tests where possible.
7. Report what changed, what was verified, what remains incomplete and known limitations.
8. Wait for direction before the next substantial step.

Do not claim that files, commits, tests, deployments, permissions or features exist unless the actual result has been checked. If a capability cannot be verified, state that clearly.

## 7. Decision status ledger

### Agreed

- Product name: Lux Omni.
- Repository: `LuxrajKayal/Luxy`.
- First development focus: the standalone web-based application interface.
- The initial workspace starts in PDF mode, with the Markdown editor opened via a dedicated action.
- Opening the Markdown editor displays PDF and Markdown panels side by side by default; users can resize them, and each panel has its own controls.
- Both iframe embedding and Web Component integration are intended future features, not initial tasks.
- Chrome extension adaptation is a later product goal, not the current focus.
- The Dropbox JavaScript SDK is loaded by the current application; its details are recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- Interface design and product wording are controlled by the owner.
- No code or assets from prior repositories may be copied into this project.

### Not yet decided

- Remaining interface appearance and detailed interaction behavior.
- Final source layout and public application/module boundaries.
- Exact iframe API, Web Component API, and which one to implement first.
- Authentication architecture and Google Drive permissions.
- Additional licensing permissions, if any, beyond the current root `LICENSE` remain subject to a separate decision.
- Release and distribution approach for the eventual commercial product.

If future conversation conflicts with this ledger, point out the conflict and ask the owner to resolve it instead of silently selecting a new direction.
